scenes.vo: What if you could talk to your computer, without making a single sound?
Voice is the fastest way to type. But in an open office, a cafe, or on a train, speaking out loud just doesn't work.
Meet Subvocal Radar. A tiny sixty gigahertz radar on a USB-C stick, inspired by The Subvocal Company.
When you silently mouth a word, your jaw and lips still move. The radar measures that motion, down to micrometres, two hundred times a second.
Inside, an Infineon radar chip with three receivers, a Raspberry Pi RP2040, and a four-layer board just seventeen by forty-six millimetres, designed end to end with my own PCB tools.
Plug it into a laptop or a phone. It shows up as a normal microphone, so it works on Windows, Android and iPhone, with no drivers.
Click any text box, hold a key, and mouth: on my way. It's typed for you. Train your own phrases in seconds.
Ready to order, fully assembled. Find it on GitHub: ajisrawi, slash, subvocal radar.
